items.title: Gradient-only proximal execution: expected pointwise work under an input moment

source.anchor: Appendix D.2, Lemma D.4 proof after equation D.7: the first Jensen expected-work inequality
source.attribution: Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang. Samplinglib isolates and expands the expectation/Jensen step; this is not the full Lemma D.4, equation D.7 or equation D.8, and is not the authors' original wording or an endorsement.

items.statement: Let an actual Algorithm D.2 query at a random center Y have pointwise count N_prox(Y) bounded by C_c[1+log(1+‖∇V(Y)‖/eps)]. If the center law is a probability measure and E‖∇V(Y)‖² is finite, then the actual count is integrable and E[N_prox(Y)]≤C_c[1+log(1+sqrt(E‖∇V(Y)‖²)/eps)]. Samplinglib constructs the measurable first-stopped execution and its count rather than assuming an accurate oracle or a cost random variable. The explicit C_c is the admissible constant already derived for D.3.
assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional complete real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure; the source specializes to Euclidean space.
V is C², kappa≥1, and kappa⁻¹‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤‖v‖² for every x,v. Fix 0<eta≤c<1 and eps>0.
nu is a probability law for the query center and y↦‖∇V(y)‖² is integrable. Lemma D.4's separate equation D.7 must later supply a uniform numerical bound for the actual Picard center laws.

obligations.label: Measurable actual Algorithm D.2 output and query count
Integrability of the realized count before taking expectation
Actual Picard center moment estimate D.7 (remaining)
Phase/call aggregation and total gradient work D.8 (remaining)

bindings.boundary: Conditional expected work for one actual stopped proximal query. No proof that the realized Picard center law satisfies D.7, no uniform C*kappa*d*L_q^18 moment bound, no 2J-per-phase/number-of-phases aggregation, no D.8, approximate-kernel stability, sampling accuracy or full-paper result. Total variation is not used to transfer unbounded cost.

assumption_deltas.source: Lemma D.4 concerns the actual Picard HMC center laws and first proves their numerical second-moment bound D.7.
assumption_deltas.lean: An arbitrary probability measure nu is allowed, under the explicit premise Integrable(y↦‖∇V(y)‖²).
assumption_deltas.reason: This isolates exactly the conditional Jensen consequence after D.7. The actual-law identification and numerical moment bound remain visible unsupported obligations, so this binding does not claim the full source lemma.

assumption_deltas.source: The source works on R^d with the normalized Hessian bounds and its stated algorithmic parameters.
assumption_deltas.lean: Finite-dimensional complete real inner-product Borel space, genuine C² Hessian bounds, kappa≥1 and full 0<eta≤c<1, eps>0.
assumption_deltas.reason: The coordinate-free domain contains the source Euclidean setting. C² prevents interpreting totalized fderiv as a derivative without regularity; the parameter range matches the parent D.3 execution theorem.

assumption_deltas.source: The proof invokes Lemma D.3's pointwise number of gradient evaluations and then Jensen's inequality.
assumption_deltas.lean: The same measurable witnesses p,N returned by the actual finite-fuel interpreter are retained; N+1 is proved integrable before integral_mono and Jensen are used.
assumption_deltas.reason: Measurability and integrability are logically required to take the displayed expectation. N+1 includes the successful residual-test query and is not a supplied cost assumption.

assumption_deltas.source: The paper writes a constant C and obtains the later bound C*L_q after inserting D.7 and parameter choices.
assumption_deltas.lean: The conditional inequality uses the explicit admissible C_c=2+(1+log((1-c)^-1))/(-log c) inherited from the formal D.3 bound.
assumption_deltas.reason: This makes the c-dependence explicit without claiming the later L_q estimate or D.8. The formula was derived in Samplinglib and is not printed verbatim in the paper.
